messages.subject: [R-SIG-Finance] TSMARCH DCC
messages.body_plain:
IThis is my first trial with tsmarch (please see the code below).
It gives me an error:

Error in set(x, j = name, value = value) :
  Supplied 5 items to be assigned to 19 items of column 'value'. If
you wish to 'recycle' the RHS please use rep() to make this intent
clear to readers of your code.


I tried to debug with ChatGPT. One suggestion was to run str(pars, max.level
= 2)
It gave:
   $ rt1: num [1:7] -7.91e-02 3.20e-01 -4.86e-02 -4.18e-01 2.17e-06 ... $
rt2: num [1:9] 5.47e-01 -6.21e-01 3.47e-06 2.14e-18 7.16e-03 ... $ : num
0.0241 $ : num 0.955 $ : num 6.19

The conclusion was:

pars list contains five elements:

   - rt1: 7 marginal-model parameters
   - rt2: 9 marginal-model parameters
   - 0.0241: DCC alpha
   - 0.955: DCC beta
   - 6.19: Student-t degrees of freedom

The asymmetry parameter gamma_1 = 0 is fixed, so it is not included among
the estimated parameters.
*The problem is that tsmarch 1.0.0 appears to be treating this mixed list
as though it were a numeric vector.* That explains why the score
calculation fails at dcc_pars/2

And that was it...
Thanks much, Alec
----------------------------------------------------------
# ARMA-GARCH-DCC for tsmarch

rm(list = ls())
library(quantmod)
library(tseries)
library(forecast)
library(tsmarch)
library(tsgarch)
library(moments)

source("C:/R/get_prices.R")
start.time <- Sys.time()
#parameters
datasource <- "Y"
version <- 1
tkr1 <- "SPY"
tkr2 <- "XLK"
startDate<-"2006-01-02"
endDate<-"2008-12-31"

ka1 <- 2
kb1 <- 2
km1 <- 1
kn1 <- 1

ka2 <- 1
kb2 <- 1
km2 <- 2
kn2 <- 2
garch1 <- "garch"
garch2 <- "gjrgarch"

DCC_outfile_name <- paste(tkr1, tkr2, garch1, garch2, ka1, kb1, km1, kn1,
                          ka2, kb2, km2, kn2,startDate, endDate, version,
sep = "-")
dcc_outfile <- paste0("C:/DCC/output/", DCC_outfile_name, ".csv")

#reading in prices
pricefile_name1 <- paste("prc",tkr1, startDate, endDate, datasource, sep =
"-")
pricefile1 <- paste0("C:/DCC/prices/", pricefile_name1, ".csv")
stat_outfile_name1 <- paste("stat",tkr1, startDate, endDate, sep = "-")
stat_outfile1 <- paste0("C:/DCC/output/", stat_outfile_name1, ".csv")

if(file.exists(pricefile1)) {
  prices1 <- read.zoo(pricefile1, sep = ",", index = 1, header = TRUE,
check.names = FALSE)
  prices1 <- as.xts(prices1)
  cat("Prices read from existing file ",pricefile1, "\n\n")
} else {
  cat("Cannot find existing price file.\n")
  prices1 <- get_prices(basket = tkr1, start = startDate, end = endDate,
datasource = datasource, outfile = pricefile1)
}

prc1 <- coredata(prices1)
rt1 <- dailyReturn(prices1)

pricefile_name2 <- paste("prc",tkr2, startDate, endDate, datasource, sep =
"-")
pricefile2 <- paste0("C:/DCC/prices/", pricefile_name2, ".csv")
stat_outfile_name2 <- paste("stat",tkr2, startDate, endDate, sep = "-")
stat_outfile2 <- paste0("C:/DCC/output/", stat_outfile_name2, ".csv")

if(file.exists(pricefile2)) {
  prices2 <- read.zoo(pricefile2, sep = ",", index = 1, header = TRUE,
check.names = FALSE)
  prices2 <- as.xts(prices2)
  cat("Prices read from existing file ",pricefile2, "\n\n")
} else {
  cat("Cannot find existing price file.\n")
  prices2 <- get_prices(basket = tkr2, start = startDate, end = endDate,
datasource = datasource, outfile = pricefile2)
}

prc2 <- coredata(prices2)
rt2 <- dailyReturn(prices2)

# Asset1:
fit1 <- garch_modelspec(
  y <- rt1,
  #returns[, "rt1"],
  model = garch1,
  order = c(km1, kn1),
  arma = c(ka1, kb1)
) |>
  estimate(keep_tmb = TRUE)

# Asset2:
fit2 <- garch_modelspec(
  #returns[, "rt2"],
  y <-rt2,
  model = garch2,
  order = c(km2, kn2),
  arma = c(ka2, kb2)
) |>
  estimate(keep_tmb = TRUE)

fits <- to_multi_estimate(list(fit1, fit2))

names(fits) <- c("rt1", "rt2")

dcc_fit <- dcc_modelspec(
  fits,
  dynamics = "dcc",
  distribution = "mvt"
) |>
  estimate()

summary(dcc_fit)

# Conditional correlation matrices
R <- tscor(dcc_fit)

# Inspect the returned object
str(R)

	[[alternative HTML version deleted]]
